tasks.short: Review the record before the visit, take the patient's eye history and complaints, type the history into the record, and check the medication list.

steps.what: Ophthalmic technologist reviews the record before the visit across several screens
Patient fills the eye history questionnaire in the patient portal before the visit
Ophthalmic technologist takes patients' medical histories and complaints
Ophthalmic technologist documents the history in the record as free text
Ophthalmic technologist checks the medication list with the patient

tasks.design: Patients fill an eye history questionnaire in the patient portal before the visit, and the answers fill structured fields in the record ({OTHER}), so the technologist confirms and adds instead of asking from scratch and typing free text. A visit summary shows earlier findings and the medication list from the national exchange, which the technologist checks with the patient. Taking the history in conversation stays with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: History was asked from scratch and typed as free text; medication was listed by memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Portals take pre-visit questionnaires; records pull medication lists from national exchanges.
tasks.still_hard: Elderly patients often skip the portal.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a 'small' complaint is a sign of something urgent.
tasks.altitude: The technologist confirms history instead of typing it.

evidence.claim: Patient portals can take pre-visit questionnaires that fill structured record fields.
Health data are special category data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the visit booked to medication checked; examination is outside.
Input contract: questionnaire linked to the record; fallback is asking and typing.

Patients fill the questionnaire before the visit (s1q, customer time). s1 keeps 70 because the summary replaces moving across screens and reading stays; s2 keeps 70 for confirming answers and asking about complaints; s3 keeps 60 because answers fill fields and the technologist still writes what the patient adds; s4 keeps 70 because the list comes from the exchange and checking it with the patient stays.
The conversation does not get shorter for patients who skip the portal.

incremental.description: No separate new work: checking answers with the patient is in s2, and the patient's time is in s1q.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many elderly patients skip the portal, so the history is taken and typed as today and s2 keeps 95, s3 keeps 90 (12.8); high: most patients fill the questionnaire (33.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Measure lens power with the lensometer, and write down and type the readings into the record.

steps.what: Ophthalmic technologist measures lens power using lensometers

Ophthalmic technologist records lens power in the record: by writing it down and typing it today, by pressing send on the lensometer and checking the reading landed on the right patient after the change

tasks.design: A digital lensometer sends sphere, cylinder, axis and add readings to the patient's record ({OTHER}) at the press of a button, so readings are not written down and typed. Measuring the glasses stays with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were written on paper and typed into the record.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital lensometers export readings to records.
tasks.still_hard: Older manual lensometers have no export.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting that a patient brought the wrong pair of glasses.

reach.learn: Whether readings are free of typing errors.

evidence.claim: Digital lensometers can export readings to patient records.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient's glasses to power recorded; prescribing is outside.
Input contract: lensometer linked to the record; fallback is writing down.
Measuring does not change. s2 keeps 20 for sending the reading and checking it is on the right patient.
research_questions: Do transcription errors in lens power fall?

incremental.description: No separate new work: checking that the reading landed on the right patient is in s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older lensometers in half of the rooms, so those readings are still written down and typed and s2 keeps 60 (16.0); high: digital lensometers in every room (32.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Measure refraction with the autorefractor, refine it with the patient, calculate corrections by hand, and record the result.

steps.what: Ophthalmic technologist measures refraction with the autorefractor
Ophthalmic technologist refines refraction with the patient
Ophthalmic technologist calculates corrections for refractive errors by hand
Ophthalmic technologist records the refraction result

tasks.design: The autorefractor and digital phoropter send their readings to the record ({OTHER}), where fixed optical formulas compute vertex distance corrections, transpositions and spherical equivalents, so the technologist does not calculate or type them. Refining refraction with the patient stays with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Corrections were calculated by hand and results typed.
tasks.enabler_now: Refraction devices export readings; records compute standard optical formulas.
tasks.human_edge: Judging which of two lenses a hesitant patient really sees better with.
tasks.altitude: The technologist refines instead of calculating.

evidence.claim: Refraction devices can export readings, and records can compute standard optical formulas.
Calculations with a medical purpose can make software a medical device; fixed optical formulas are validated before use.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient seated to the result recorded; prescribing is outside.
Input contract: devices linked to the record; fallback is calculating by hand.

incremental.description: Ophthalmic technologist checks computed corrections on unusual prescriptions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: manual phoropters in many rooms, so refined results are still typed and s4 keeps 70 (20.5); high: linked digital devices (24.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take triage calls and ask about symptoms, look up the triage protocol, decide urgency, and book the appointment and record the triage.

steps.what: Ophthalmic technologist performs ophthalmic triage by phone, asking about symptoms
Ophthalmic technologist looks up the triage protocol in a binder
Ophthalmic technologist assesses severity of patients' conditions
Ophthalmic technologist books the appointment and records the triage

tasks.design: The clinic's triage protocol is built into a triage form in the record ({OTHER}) with the protocol's questions and urgency categories, so the technologist does not look it up in a binder. The urgency the technologist chooses opens the matching slot list, so the agenda is not searched; the technologist books the slot and saves the form as the triage record. Asking about symptoms and deciding urgency stay with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: The protocol sat in a binder and triage was noted separately from booking.
tasks.enabler_now: Records hold triage forms linked to slot lists.
tasks.still_hard: Vague symptoms do not fit the protocol's questions.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing panic in a caller's voice that the symptoms list misses.

reach.learn: Whether urgent cases are seen on time.

evidence.claim: Records can hold triage forms linked to appointment slot lists.
Software that decides urgency for a medical purpose can be a medical device; here the technologist decides.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient call to the triage recorded; the visit is outside.
Input contract: protocol built into the form; fallback is the binder.

Asking and deciding urgency keep their full time. s2 keeps 40 for reading the protocol questions in the form; s4 keeps 70 because the slot list replaces searching the agenda, and booking and recording stay.
research_questions: Do urgent patients get slots faster?

incremental.description: Ophthalmic technologist reports protocol gaps to the ophthalmologist.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many calls fall outside the form's questions, so the binder is still used and s2 keeps 70, s4 keeps 85 (5.5); high: the form covers most calls (11.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The ophthalmic technologist keeps taking histories, measuring, refining refraction and triaging; typed history, written readings, hand calculations and binder look-ups shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technologist with more time with patients.
